messages.subject: Re: peptide PTM annotation and sequence
messages.body_plain:
Hi Robin,

I know that the output of the function "groupComparisonPTM" contains the exact location of the PTM on the protein (e.g. if you see Q9UHD8_K262 in the protein column, this  means that lysine was modified at site 262 for protein Q9UHD8).

To get the centered amino acid sequence surrounding the PTM site, my first thought is that you can download a FASTA file from Uniprot <https://www.uniprot.org/id-mapping> containing all of the proteins of interest in your dataset.  MSstatsPTM has a function called "tidyFasta" which takes your FASTA file and imports it as a data table containing the sequence for each protein.  Then, you can find the amino acid sequence surrounding the PTM site using some additional R code.

Here's a code example below with Q9UHD8_K262:

library(dplyr)
fasta_data_table = tidyFasta("fasta filepath")
fasta_row = filter(fasta_data_table, uniprot_ac == "Q9UHD8")
amino_acid_sequence = substring(fasta_row$sequence, 257, 267) # taking the 10 amino acids surrounding K262.

In summary, MSstatsPTM does not completely support your situation out of the box, but there's ways to write R code to make this work seamlessly.  Let me know if you have any other questions or need any additional clarifications.

Thanks,
Tony

messages.subject: MSstatsPTM removing unmodified peptides
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I was wondering if you could offer any advice on what to do with unmodified peptides in a PTM-enriched dataset when performing MSstatsPTM.

Briefly, I have a diGly enriched proteome and a whole peptide proteome which were run separately. The whole peptide proteome datasets was analysed using MSstatsTMT, and both datasets were analysed using MSstatsPTM. For MSstatsPTM, the whole peptide proteome was utilised as the 'unmodified dataset' which is being used to adjust against the diGly enriched dataset during the groupComparisonPTM stage (as recommended in the paper).

This is working well for MSstatsPTM, however it does mean I end up with both diGly modified and unmodified peptides that were present in the diGly enriched proteome. As I am only interested in the diGly modified peptides when performing MSstatsPTM, these peptides are of no value.

I was wondering what the best course of action is for removing these unmodified peptides.

1. Should they be removed at all?
2. If they can be removed, when is it best to remove them i.e. should they be removed before protein summarisation, or before groupComparisonPTM or should they be left until after MSstatsPTM analysis is performed and then removed after.

At the moment I have removed the unmodified peptides after protein summarisation by using this code:

MSstats.SF.diGly.Protein <- quant.msstats.SF$PTM[["ProteinLevelData"]]
MSstats.SF.diGly.Protein <- MSstats.SF.diGly.Protein %>% filter(str_detect(Protein, "_"))

Essentially this removes data without any '_' symbol, which you only get if it is followed by a diGly site e.g. Ttn would be removed and Ttn_K6 would be kept.

Any advice on what the best approach and best time to removing unmodified peptides would be greatly appreciated :)

Many thanks

Sam

messages.body_plain:
Dear Tony,

In attach I added the annotation file and a subset of the data file.

Note that I also needed to clean up/edit the data file a bit before MSstatsPTM could handle it, this is the code I use for that:
raw_data_EDIT$V12 = NULL
colnames(raw_data_EDIT) = raw_data_EDIT[1,]
raw_data_EDIT = raw_data_EDIT[-1,]

#remove rows without PTM, exclude 1st row which is part of the header
header_1 = raw_data_EDIT[1,]
raw_data_EDIT = raw_data_EDIT[!(raw_data_EDIT$X.9==""), ]
raw_data_EDIT = rbind(header_1, raw_data_EDIT)

#remove accessions that are not sp|UniProtID|geneID_MOUSE format
header_2 = raw_data_EDIT[2,]
raw_data_EDIT = raw_data_EDIT[ grepl("_MOUSE", raw_data_EDIT$X.10, fixed = TRUE),]    #gets rid of other species and CON-MOUSE
raw_data_EDIT = raw_data_EDIT[!grepl("*_sp", raw_data_EDIT$X.10, fixed = F),]         #gets rid of decoy hits (REV_sp)
raw_data_EDIT = rbind(header_1, header_2, raw_data_EDIT)

annotation_data_PTM = read.csv("phospho_annotation.csv", sep = ",")
msstatsPTM_input = ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat(raw_data_EDIT,
                                                annotation = annotation_data_PTM )
#renaming 1 column because name is wrong, this is due to ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat being an old converter
names(msstatsPTM_input$PTM)[names(msstatsPTM_input$PTM) == 'PeptideModifiedSequence'] <- 'PeptideSequence'

After these steps, I can run dataSummarizationPTM (with or without added total proteomics data).

Kind regards,

Robin

messages.subject: Re: A lot of NA
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alice,

This is a challenging question to answer without more information.

Are most of these NAs on the precursor or fragment level, or are entire proteins missing?

If the missingness is at the precursor or fragment-level you might be able to get away with simply using the imputation methods in MSstats (although I would check the imputed values to ensure they make sense).

If the missing values are at the protein-level, I personally do not believe there is a great way to recover them. You can make assumptions, such as the proteins are below the limit of detection, but you are moving away from quantitative analysis and toward qualitative analysis when you do this.

Devon

Sam
